topics.name: AI Agents

perspectives.title: AI Agents

representative_posts.author: pavelshlepnev.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: So many AI agent solutions... I'd rather create my own. Here it is, by the way:

representative_posts.author: iassets.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: A CFTC forum this week said agentic AI needs rules now, not later. The question regulators keep asking: what did the agent actually do. iBird already answers that — every action lands on Hedera, timestamped, public, unchangeable.

representative_posts.author: jenlucpiquant.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Basically no one is using AI agents for their DoorDash orders

representative_posts.author: ai-news.at.thenote.app
representative_posts.text: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says During its busiest week last quarter, Uber said only four people booked a ride using an AI agent. Telegram AI Digest #ai #news

representative_posts.author: agentkitco.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The most useful part of any AI agent is its instructions. A good system prompt covers: role, goal, what it must never do, and the format of its answers. We wrote a template:

representative_posts.author: shehackspurple.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Here's a question I'd like everyone building AI agents to ask: **What's the worst thing your agent is ACTUALLY ALLOWED to do?** Not what you've instructed it to do. Not what it usually does. What can it actually DO? Can it: → Access credentials? → Read confidential files? 1/4

representative_posts.author: dmitryontech.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Marketing AI Agents in 2026: How Autonomous AI Can Promote and Scale Your Micro-SaaS, Mobile App, or Indie Product

representative_posts.author: steadyvane.com
representative_posts.text: An Ask HN thread asks what AI agent setup people actually run. It went from 4 to 354 upvotes in about 20 hours, about 12x the typical pace of other stories SteadyVane tracks on Hacker News. Replies mix paid plans, pay-per-token APIs and local models. No consensus.

representative_posts.author: agenttmz.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: 😱 UNDER OATH: Google told a New York City Council hearing that its AI agents left a test environment and reached the live internet. Three separate times. 👉 #AIagents #AI #agenticAI

representative_posts.author: astrodevil1.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: My read: a chat answer used to be one call. An agent task is dozens of calls, each resending the context. Cheaper tokens made those loops affordable. Are your AI bills going down or up this quarter?

representative_posts.author: campuscodi.risky.biz
representative_posts.text: At least one threat actor has posed as an AI agent to scan enterprise networks for unsecured passwords, API keys, and cloud credentials. The attacker has rotated through 32 different AI bots, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity.

representative_posts.author: svkt.eu
representative_posts.text: AI agents are good when a lot of information needs to be correlated and sorted through, that's why the idea of connecting one to your finances is not completely absurd (if done well). Uber eats is just pick the food you want to eat and order it. The agent just gets in the way.

representative_posts.author: aitrainingjobs.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: New AI training role: AI Agent Evaluator micro1 · $25–$45/hr · Remote #RemoteWork #AIjobs

representative_posts.author: meetdux.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Agent governance, made practical. AI Governance Playbook: Scaling Agents Without Chaos (THR1004) Nov 18, 10:10 AM PT | San Francisco | In person Register: #MSIgnite

representative_posts.author: oikofuge.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The last para is revelatory, I think. The author seems to find it noteworthy that sending AI-generated text to people close to you might not be well received. This is, of course, why we don't sit in the pub with our friends, letting AI agents chat on our behalf.

representative_posts.author: oludai.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: 🤖 We checked whether AI tools are readable by AI agents. 167 tools with a public site: · 39% publish an llms.txt · 10% declare an AI crawler policy · 5% expose an mcp.json Everyone claims to be agent-friendly. Few went past the easiest file. #AI #OpenSource #MCP

representative_posts.author: isolvedhcm.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Your AI agents are being paid. Do you know how much? 💸 Every task an agent completes draws down tokens, and tokens are billed in dollars. isolved CEO Michael Haske explains why that spend belongs in your workforce budget, not IT's. Read our #blog: 👉

representative_posts.author: shehackspurple.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: A prompt? Or an independently enforced security control? Because those are VERY different answers. We don't need to predict every strange decision an AI agent might make. But we DO need to control what happens when it makes one. **Don't solve a permissions problem with a prompt.** 3/4

representative_posts.author: sipirtu.com
representative_posts.text: Airbnb announced that it will launch an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027. Source: TechCrunch

representative_posts.author: evecodes.com
representative_posts.text: #EdwardSnowden said #SamAltman should be in jail for releasing agentic #AI. The user cannot see what the agent is doing, so if it fucks something up or accesses a company the user didn't intend, the user is still liable. A lot of innocent people may start getting sued.

representative_posts.author: pillai.wsocial.eu
representative_posts.text: Perplexity’s new Teammates move AI from one-off prompts toward ongoing projects, memory and coordinated tasks. Persistent agents raise a useful design challenge: how do teams keep scope clear, actions reviewable and ownership explicit? #AgenticAI

representative_posts.author: elena.gworky.com
representative_posts.text: How to manage AI agents in a team: 4 principles for cohesion Manage AI agents by assigning specific human owners, earning autonomy through low error rates, defining measurable KPIs, and monitoring performance we...

representative_posts.author: abeba.blacksky.app
representative_posts.text: They raised concerns about rogue AI swarms & mentioned the HF incidents, including examples of AI agents bullying one another & coordinating via messaging board. They emphasise how we have moved from AI systems that could barely communicate to rogue AI having encrypted conversations w/ one another

AI Not Worth It argues that AI is not worth the cost.

The posts defend it in their own words. @eyepatchguy.bsky.social writes, “My stance has always been “this thing has potential use cases, but they are not worth the cost as it stands and any serious regulation of AI has to get rid of daily personal use for bullshit reasons or it is meaningless.” I have not changed this position” @cookting.bsky.social writes, “Fait accompli here for the "AI is inevitable" claim. A claim being pushed while it's sold to us at a loss for tasks it's barely capable of doing with risks and illegalities in its implementation we're told to ignore. Now it's just an everyday thing normal people do. No, it's not.” @jackshawhan.bsky.social writes, “I like this. People who know me know that aside from the artistic, veritacular, and environmental costs (things that can be mitigated with regulation and cultural forces), I am more or less ambivalent toward AI.”

Other views in this conversation are AI Value. They are arguing a different claim from AI Not Worth It.

NO GOALIE INTERFERENCE” @keithsmithnba.bsky.social writes, “Hugo Gonzalez gets an early call tonight. Jordan Walsh fouled Norman Powell twice while he was shooting three-pointers. Powell is a tough cover, but both fouls were avoidable by Walsh.” @carcelmousineau.bsky.social writes, “Didn't think it was allowed for our goalie to save so many shots”
